newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SCA says good demand for hygiene products.
newsitem.headline: SCA says good demand for hygiene products.

text.p: Swedish forestry group SCA said on Monday it saw continued positive growth in its hygiene products business area and continued improvement in earnings in packaging operations but at a slower rate.
"Continued strong demand is expected for SCA's hygiene products but with increasing pressure on prices and increasing raw materials costs," the company said in its first quarter earnings statement.
"Sales of corrugated board should gradually benefit from increased industrial production in Europe."
SCA posted a 12 percent fall in first quarter profit after financial items to 894 million crowns from the corresponding quarter a year earlier, including a capital gain of 125 million crowns.
The profit was lower than expected with analysts in a Reuter poll targeting 950 million crowns and the report triggering a fall in SCA's share price.

At 1345 GMT, the share was down six crowns or 3.5 percent at 166 while the general index was 1.84 percent lower at 2,564.57. Before the report was released the share was changing hands at 170.5 crowns, down 1.5.

The lower profit shows the company has continued to suffer from the sluggish forestry trends that started in the autumn of 1995 when an inventory build-up caused demand to dwindle and prices to plunge.
Although prices have picked up lately, price trends were mixed, the company said.
"The decline in prices for wood-containing paper and pulp continued during the quarter while prices and volume of business in fine papers increased substantially," SCA said.
It added that increases in liner prices had been announced.
Sales fell four percent to 14.22 billion crowns and the main part of the decrease, three percentage points, was attributed to divestments of non-core operations. But sales volumes grew 10 percent.
Furthermore, first quarter 1997 sales were four percent higher than in the fourth quarter of 1996, the company said.

Operating profit fell 11 percent to 1.13 billion crowns and included a capital gain of 125 million crowns on the sale of Industrivarden shares. Earnings per share fell to 2.62 crowns from 3.07 crowns.
